### [S023.U3] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.5 CEMENT MATERIALS
- C. The following other types of cement may be used in Work if specified or with prior approval of the ER in writing purpose. Specialist literature shall be consulted for guidance regarding use of these types of cement.
1. 43 Grade ordinary Portland cement conforming to IS 8112
2. 53 Grade ordinary Portland cement conforming to IS 12269
3. Portland slag cement conforming to IS 455

4. Portland pozzolana cement (fly ash based ) conforming to IS 1489 (Part-I)
5. Portland pozzolana cement (calcined clay based ) conforming to IS 1489 (Pt -2)
6. Sulphate resisting Portland cement conforming to IS 12330

### [S026.U3] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.7 ADMIXTURES FOR CONCRETE
- D. Fly Ash: Shall conform to IS 3812 (Parts I and II) or ASTM C618, Class C or F except limit lignite ignition to maximum of 6% with maximum of (220kg/m 3 ). No additives or contaminants derived from the fly ash precipitation process that are detrimental to concrete (such as soda ash) are permitted. The fly ash producer shall have a minimum of 5 years' experience in the production of acceptable fly ash and shall maintain an effective quality control program to guard against contamination of the fly ash.
- E. Other Admixtures: Use only with the prior written approval of the ER. Do not use any admixtures which contain chlorides or sulphates.
- F. Compatibility of multiple admixtures, including fly ash, used in the same mix shall be certified

### [S027.U12] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE
Note :-1The Presence of mica in the fine aggregate has been found to reduce considerably the durability and compressive strength of concrete and further investigations are underway to determine and extent of the deleterious effect of mica. It is advisable, therefore, to investigate the mica content of fine aggregate and make suitable allowance for the possible reduction in the strength of concrete mortar.

Note :-2 The aggregate shall not contain harmful organic impurities (tested in accordance with IS : 2386 [part - ii]) in sufficient quantities to affect adversely the strength or durability of concrete. A fine aggregate which fails in the test for organic impurities may be used, provided that, when tested for the effect of organic impurities on the strength of mortar, the relative strength at 7 and 28 days, reported in accordance with 7 of IS : 2386 [ Part - VI] - 1963 is not less than 95% percent.

### [S033.U1] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.10 CURING MATERIALS
- A. ASTM C1315. Water-based acrylic coating suitable for concrete curing and surface sealing. Clear transparent, low odor, high solids content. Section 12.5 of SP 24 shall also be followed.

### [S034.U1] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.11 REQUIREMENTS FOR MASS CONCRETE
- A. Mass concrete clauses shall apply to concrete used in Mat Foundations and should be considered for footings greater than 1.0 m thick. Same materials and proportioning as normal weight structural concrete, except use moderate heat of hydration, moderate sulphate resistance cement, water reducing retarding admixture, and crushed ice if necessary to maintain required temperature.

1. Retardation: Minimum 3 hours.
2. Temperature: Maximum 21° C at point of deposit.

### [S049.U4] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > B. Cement Concrete.
- c. The Contractor shall ensure that the minimum cement content per cubic

- meter of reinforced concrete should not be less than that stipulated in table 23, 24, 25 and 26 of SP 23 and Table 5 and Table 6 herein.
- d. For expected strength of cubes tested on the 28 th day the design mix at preliminary test and work site shall be as per IS 456, SP 23 and SP 24. The water cement ratio shall be between 0.5 to 0.52. Additional water may be permitted only at the discretion of the ER. The slump shall be 25 mm to 35 mm depending upon the location and type of Work. Higher slump with use of plasticizers shall be permitted.

### [S049.U15] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
6. Retempering: No water shall be added to the mix after the initial batching operation. Concrete which is placed after the unauthorized addition of water is subject to removal.
7. When required, the slump of concrete as delivered to the site may be increased prior to placement by the use of a high range water reducing admixture. Dosage of superplasticizer shall be within the guidelines established by the manufacturer and agreed to by the ER. Alternative Mix Design Reports with the recommended site dosage(s) of superplasticizer shall be submitted prior to use.

### [S049.U16] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
8. The placing temperature of concrete shall not be more than 34 o C. If it is more, the ER may order addition of ice or chilled water to the concrete at no additional cost to the Employer. Also the Contractor shall take the following precautions:
- a. Mixers and weight batches shall be painted with white colour
- b. Aggregate storing bins shall not be exposed to the Sun.
- c. Water shall be sprinkled on aggregates well before concreting to keep the temperature low.

### [S050.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > E. Shrinkage cracks
1. Concreting shall be avoided in very warm weather, if necessary, it shall be covered with dampened Hessian within 2 hours of placing of concrete.
2. To achieve good results the concrete shall be immediately covered with a plastic sheet and not exposed to any direct wind contact.

### [S060.U9] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING > b. Three cubes shall be tested on the 7 th day and other three cube...
- e. Compression Test Reports: Present at least the following data in tabular form and distribute immediately after recording the test results.
- 1) Identity of job, Contractor, supplier.
- 2) Identity of mix and required strength.
- 3) Pour location of sampled concrete.
- 4) Slump, water content, air content, truck number, time and date sampled, air temperature, concrete temperature, consistency.

### [S060.U10] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING > b. Three cubes shall be tested on the 7 th day and other three cube...
- 5) Curing history.
- 6) Date tested.
- 7) Compressive strength.
- 8) Type of fracture.
- 9) Compliance with specifications (yes or no)
- F. Slump Tests: First truck each day, each sample for cylinders, and as often as necessary thereafter. Provide a slump cone and rod available for use at all times. Verify water content in accordance with AASHTO T318, "Measurement of Water Content of Fresh Concrete Using the Microwave Oven" as required by the ER, but not less than one test per day.
